score_note: BQS 5.18; raw Growth Quality 6.75 capped at 5 by persistent CASH 2. Medium confidence for quality; IAS NS because funding, collections and BSE execution are unresolved.

GOV.reason: Detailed disclosure and approved IPO reallocation are positives. Related receivables, turnover-based commission, audit-log gaps and payment delays limit assurance. March no-pledge declaration is dated, not current clearance; no severe abuse established.

MOAT.reason: Execution credentials and PSU relationships support repeat bids. Increasing concentration, tender economics and permissions constrain pricing power; CBG economics remain unproven.

REV.reason: Five-year sales CAGR53.98% maps to 9, capped at 8 for medium confidence. Acquired SGAEPL had nil historic turnover. Contract-asset growth and free-issue-material mix qualify economic comparability; no extra trajectory uplift.

DUR.reason: Substantial dated backlog and utility infrastructure demand support multi-year work. Rights-of-way, customer billing and financing constrain conversion. The MoU and Rs 1000 crore ambition are not contracted revenue.

CAP.reason: Accounting incremental NOPAT/invested-capital proxy is about 16.3%, supporting a moderate score. Most added capital sits in unbilled work, retention and receivables; realized cash returns are much weaker. No persistent CAP<=3 override.

CASH.reason: Four consecutive negative-CFO years and rising unbilled/retention claims establish persistent weak conversion. Supplier finance improves reported CFO by Rs 4 crore; a financing reclassification makes operating cash worse. Rapid growth explains funding demand, not cash generation.

BAL.reason: Moderate debt/EBITDA and investment-grade rating are positives. Cash below Rs 1 crore, pledged FD,89% bank utilization and expensive NBFC loans leave liquidity stretched despite substantial equity.

EXEC.reason: Sales/core-profit growth and phase 1 commissioning are real. Cash promises remain unfulfilled,1TPD is below the 2TPD target, and customer concentration increases. Mixed execution, not a promotional score.

EARN.reason: Core EBIT and owner profit grew strongly with little other-income support. Medium confidence caps at 8; completion-based recognition and unbilled assets require collection validation. Persistent CASH weakness caps composite Growth Quality.

R.reason: Large unbilled/retention balances lack independently verified acceptance and collection schedules; current facility headroom and optional CBG funding are not established. These affect achievable growth, funding survival and recoverable equity. Full annual core/expansion/impairment cases are supplied, but low-confidence economic inputs prevent point factors; absence of an official BSE price alone is not the reason. Audit opinion is unmodified and cash reconciles. Completion-based revenue and large unbilled claims require collection validation. Supplier-finance classification is explicit, not missing cash; no critical reliability hold is inferred solely from drafting errors.

Contract-asset collection and additional facility availability are essential to fund growth and optional CBG expansion. sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Strong reported EPC growth is real, but cash conversion dominates the investment case. FY2026 revenue doubled to Rs 118.61 crore and owner PAT reached Rs 16.35 crore, while CFO was negative Rs 19.03 crore. Unbilled work of Rs 44.04 crore and retention of Rs 8.38 crore absorb funding. Supplier finance contributes Rs 4 crore within reported CFO. Watch for billing and collections before treating reported growth as investable growth. [S1][S4]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Desco Infratech Limited, BSE SME 544387, ISIN INE0TGG01014, was incorporated in 2011 and listed on April 1, 2025. It is primarily an EPC and maintenance contractor, not a regulated gas utility. FY2026 group accounts include 99%-held BioGreen and 75%-held SGAEPL; the UAE entity was inactive. Verified shares 7,676,008; official lot 500. Cutoff October 20, 2026; five-year horizon, 15% nominal pretax hurdle and ₹5 lakh reference position. October 19 secondary close ₹170.95; lot value ₹85,475. All 60 secondary dates are observed without zero filling. Historical quality confidence is medium; current contract collections, funding and CBG economics are low-confidence valuation inputs. All four gates are Conditional, not evidenced critical failures. [S1][S6][S12][S16]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS 5.18 and raw Growth Quality 6.75 use canonical weights. Persistent CASH 2 caps Growth Quality at 5. IAS is NS. The audit opinion is unmodified and closing cash reconciles, but large contract assets require collection validation. Explained bank-statement reconciliation and an immaterial ageing typo do not trigger a critical reliability hold. [S1][S3] Conditional L is now 5 from 60 dated secondary observations; IAS remains NS for specific operating/funding gaps, not unavailable market history.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The company executes and maintains city-gas, water, power and renewable-support infrastructure. AS7 revenue recognizes project completion, supported by engineer certification before customer billing. Private clients may supply materials free, whereas PSU projects can require procurement: reported revenue is not constant value-added output. Subcontractor execution, customer acceptance, retention and financing determine cash economics. CBG adds a different operating model whose feedstock, offtake and utilization remain to be proven. [S1][S3][S4]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Promoter experience, prequalification and repeat customer relationships support credible access to tenders, not monopoly pricing. The rating agency reports top-five customer concentration rising from 41% to 71%; SunDrops alone contributes 33%. Permissions, rights-of-way, weather and client certification can delay payment despite reputed counterparties. Overseas ventures and the DenEB MoU are opportunities, not demonstrated competitive advantages. [S3][S5][S11]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Revenue was Rs 13.70 crore in FY2021, then Rs 19.85/29.22/29.39/59.45/118.61 crore in FY2022–26. Five-year CAGR is 53.98%, mapping to REV 8 after the medium-confidence cap. Acquired SGAEPL had nil historical turnover, so purchased revenue does not explain the acceleration. RHP restatement explicitly bridges FY2024 book PAT of Rs 3.3214 crore to Rs 3.4580 crore through gratuity, prior-period and tax adjustments. Latest core EBIT rose from Rs 13.12 crore to Rs 23.22 crore, although power/solar mix reduced margins. [S1][S2][S3][S6]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The rating agency reports March backlog of Rs 339.72 crore, 2.86 times sales, with CGD comprising 74%. The May call’s Rs 345 crore backlog is a different snapshot and must not be silently merged. Management’s 70–80% growth and Rs 1,000 crore sales ambition require funding and certification improvements, not simply market demand. June commissioning delivered 1 TPD of CBG capacity versus the May target of 2 TPD; ultimate design is 5 TPD and sales were still pending. The September DenEB MoU has no fixed financial commitment or booked order. [S4][S5][S7][S11] The May call additionally discussed roughly ₹25 crore for proposed Gujarat/Madhya Pradesh CBG projects. This is a management expansion ambition, not established funded capex; full annual funding sensitivities include it without inventing incremental plant earnings. [S4]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: Promoters hold 58.31%. Related external sales are Rs 13.10 crore, 11.05% of revenue, but related receivables of Rs 7.00 crore represent 23% of total debtors. Actual remuneration is separated from the shareholder-approved increase in CMD commission from 0.3% to 1% of turnover, effective October 2026; sales-linked pay can outpace cash realization. The Rs 1.6804 crore machinery-to-working-capital IPO variation was shareholder-approved. Fixed-asset audit-log limitations, statutory-payment delays and the unscheduled subsidiary loan require stronger controls. Subsidiary sales authorizations of Rs 30 crore each are not external orders. [S1][S8][S9] March primary shareholding declares no pledge or other promoter encumbrance, but this is not October clearance. [S10] The 9 October voting filing confirms approval at the 7 October AGM; actual payout remains unverified. [S15]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: CFO was negative in each of FY2023–26. Two-year CFO/PAT is about −1.226 times; FY2026 reported FCF is −Rs 21.90 crore before capital advances. Closing cash of Rs 0.7938 crore reconciles. Reported CFO includes Rs 3.9992 crore of supplier-finance draw: moving this financing-like inflow below operating cash produces a sensitivity of −Rs 23.0309 crore, without changing total cash. Other current assets include Rs 44.04 crore of unbilled work and Rs 8.38 crore of retention; management describes 36–48 month defect-liability retention periods. Engineer-certified work is not yet accepted billing. The ageing schedule shows about Rs 3.60 crore over six months with no provision, despite a contradictory summary heading. Its Rs 0.007 crore sum mismatch is immaterial. [S1][S3][S4]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: The October 19 secondary close of ₹170.95 replaces the October 12 ₹176 reference. Market capitalization is ₹131.22 crore and current-share owner P/E approximately 8.03×. Actual operating WC is ₹76.7578 crore, gross debt ₹15.4719 crore and cash ₹0.7938 crore. Full annual core EPC cases assume 10/25/40% growth, pre-incremental-commission EBITDA margins 15/19/21%, WC 72/62/52% and 6/9/12× exit EBITDA. Higher approved commission, replacement/growth capex, CBG completion reserves and simultaneous gross borrowing interest are explicitly funded.  Optional ₹25 crore new CBG plans, claim impairment, completion costs and minority allocation receive full annual sensitivities; they are not omitted or assumed funded. IAS remains NS for contract acceptance/current-facility and plant-economics gaps. [S1][S4][S5][S7][S15][S16] Model correction dated 20 October 2026: the earlier forecast omitted certain opening liabilities excluded from operating working capital. The revised model pays opening net tax and other current claims once, preserves actual opening assets/debt, and leaves employee provisions already captured in working capital unchanged. This corrects our forecast, not the issuer’s financial statements. No liability is paid twice through working capital, debt, capex or recurring compensation. Corrected bear/base/bull terminal prices are ₹161.81/₹696.01/₹1904.23; corresponding five-year returns are -1.09%/32.42%/61.95%. These remain conditional operating and funding scenarios, not executable entry prices. Opening-claim amounts, timing alternatives and annual cash/debt checks are in the model. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: A 20% impairment of unbilled plus retention claims would be ₹10.48 crore before tax, approximately 64% of FY2026 owner PAT. This is a stress, not an observed loss. The full severe annual case contracts revenue 10% per year, uses 8% EBITDA margin before incremental commission, WC of 85% of revenue, 4× terminal EBITDA and explicit completion/optional-expansion cash. Impairment reduces usable opening WC, is a noncash earnings charge/addback, and requires replacement funding once through delta WC. A conservative 25% terminal economic allocation stress is not actual minority ownership of every group asset. Customer certification delays, expensive refinancing and dilution can cause permanent loss despite accounting earnings. Conversely, accepted billing and collection could release substantial funding. Secondary low×volume capacity is not executable depth or BSE surveillance clearance. [S1][S4][S5][S12][S16]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold appreciation in five years requires 38.0% annual per-share compounding; tenfold requires 58.5%. Historical reported sales growth has reached those rates, but sustainable cash returns have not. Upside needs orders to become accepted bills and cash, better funding terms, retention release, profitable CBG utilization and limited dilution. No multibagger probability is assigned.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Track unbilled ageing, engineer certification versus customer acceptance, subsequent billing and collections, and retention release. Obtain CFO excluding supplier finance and a debt roll-forward; test the cash-conversion promise in FY2027–28. Monitor SunDrops and related-party payments, NBFC refinancing, bank utilization and FD liens. Confirm CBG saleable output, offtake and feedstock economics. Verify actual commission payout, current pledges, audit-log remediation and official BSE liquidity before sizing. [S1][S4][S5][S7][S9]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Deep quality review with a persistent cash-conversion constraint. BQS and capped Growth Quality are supported at medium confidence; IAS is not rankable. Hold for cash validation, not because growth is absent. Historical statements, governance, forensics, acquisition scope, capital structure and annual scenarios were substantially reviewed. Remaining gaps are explicit. This research does not execute a trade.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Reviewed primary issuer reports, FY2022 accounts, the primary RHP mirrored by Dhan, dated exchange filings, management call and rating rationale. Issuer and merchant RHP links failed; the legitimate mirror was recovered. Historical restatements are reconciled rather than treated as automatic red flags. The price is a dated October 19 secondary close. Official BSE execution and surveillance, current CBG sales, contract-asset collections and freely available deposits remain unverified. [S1][S2][S3][S5][S13] Original FY2024 audit wording is internally inconsistent about gratuity qualification; the RHP restatement and current actuarial disclosures were checked rather than carrying an old paragraph forward as a current qualification. [S14]

notes: March cash/debt/WC are actual note-built balances. No IPO proceeds are added again; original and varied IPO uses are not separate operating expenses on top of delta WC.

Core revenue scenarios are EPC operating cases, not a fabricated CBG revenue forecast. Revenue-linked capex remains 4/4/4.5%, plus an explicit ₹3 crore remaining-existing-CBG completion reserve. This is an analyst assumption, not verified expenditure guidance; ₹0–5 crore sensitivity is supplied. Already recorded capital advances/CWIP are not paid again.

May call discussed additional Gujarat/Madhya Pradesh CBG projects totaling roughly ₹25 crore. These are not established funded commitments. Full annual sensitivities add ₹25 crore over FY2027–28 with no invented incremental CBG earnings; severe case also includes it. Delaying/cancelling expansion is a real alternative to debt assumed in these cases.

Margins are before incremental CMD commission. The approved increase from 0.3% to 1% turnover from October 2026 is modeled as extra 0.35% revenue in FY2027 and 0.7% thereafter. Actual payment is not yet observed.

Interest is 12% times opening gross debt plus half of draws minus half of repayments, solved with 25% positive cash tax. Cash floor ₹0.5 crore. New facilities are conditional; current high utilization means modeled draws cannot be treated as assured funding.
Claim impairment reduces usable opening WC and is a noncash earnings charge/addback; replacement funding enters delta WC once, without a second cash write-off or assumed tax relief.

Terminal EV equals EBITDA times multiple, then add cash and subtract debt. Primary core cases assume no incremental CBG earnings or value and no minority deduction from that core value. Separate 25% economic-haircut sensitivity is a deliberately conservative group-allocation stress, not a claim that all group assets have that minority ownership. No terminal collateral salvage or dividend.
